## Question and data

This descriptive analysis summarizes BMI and age by `IncomeGroup` in the
prepared NHANES Health Equity classroom snapshot. The CSV is loaded from a
relative repository path so the analysis can be rerun in a fresh Codespace.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)

# AI prompt: Help structure a rerunnable relative-path EDA for the supplied CSV.
# Verified: The path exists from the repository root, and these variables are
# present with numeric Age and BMI columns.
data_path <- "examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv"
if (!file.exists(data_path)) {
  stop("Expected dataset was not found at: ", data_path)
}

nhanes <- read_csv(data_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Analysis cohort

The intended cohort is adults ages 20 through 80, inclusive. The age filter is
applied before any summary statistics. Missing values are not silently treated
as zeros; the missingness report below is produced first, and records missing
`BMI`, `Age`, or `IncomeGroup` are excluded only for the corresponding complete
case Table 1.

```{r}
#| label: cohort
# AI prompt: Verify that the required age range is inclusive and that exclusions
# are explicit before the descriptive summary.
# Verified: `between(Age, 20, 80)` includes both endpoints; the later filter
# excludes only variables required by Table 1.
cohort <- nhanes |>
  filter(between(Age, 20, 80))

tibble(
  dataset = c("Full CSV", "Age 20-80 cohort"),
  n = c(nrow(nhanes), nrow(cohort))
) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Stage", "N"))
```

## Missingness

Missingness is checked for every variable used in the cohort definition or
Table 1 before interpreting group summaries.

```{r}
#| label: missingness
key_variables <- c("Age", "BMI", "IncomeGroup")

missingness <- tibble(
  variable = key_variables,
  missing_n = vapply(nhanes[key_variables], function(x) sum(is.na(x)), integer(1)),
  total_n = nrow(nhanes)
) |>
  mutate(missing_percent = round(100 * missing_n / total_n, 1))

kable(
  missingness,
  col.names = c("Variable", "Missing N", "Total N", "Missing (%)"),
  caption = "Missingness in the full prepared CSV"
)
```

## Table 1-style descriptive summary

The Table 1 uses complete records for `Age`, `BMI`, and `IncomeGroup` within
the age-defined cohort. `N` is the number of records contributing to both
means. Standard deviation is calculated with `sd()`, not variance.

```{r}
#| label: table1
# AI prompt: Draft a Table 1 grouped by IncomeGroup with N and mean (SD).
# Verified: I checked the output against the complete-case filter and confirmed
# that the parenthesized values are standard deviations calculated by `sd()`.
table1_data <- cohort |>
  filter(
    !is.na(Age),
    !is.na(BMI),
    !is.na(IncomeGroup)
  )

table1 <- table1_data |>
  group_by(IncomeGroup) |>
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    `BMI, mean (SD)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(BMI), sd(BMI)),
    `Age, mean (SD)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(Age), sd(Age)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(IncomeGroup)

kable(
  table1,
  caption = "Table 1. Descriptive characteristics by income group"
)

write_csv(table1, "assignments/assignment06-eda-ai-audit/submission/table1.csv")
```

## Methods note

We analyzed the prepared NHANES Health Equity classroom CSV snapshot and
defined the cohort as records with age 20–80 inclusive. We reported missingness
for age, BMI, and income group before excluding records missing any of those
variables from the Table 1 summary. We summarized the complete-case cohort
with N, BMI mean (SD), and age mean (SD) by `IncomeGroup` using unweighted
descriptive statistics. This analysis describes the prepared classroom
dataset only and is not a causal analysis or a population-representative
estimate.
